correctness.rationale: The pair (B_q,X_q) gives the W-equivariant short exact sequence; explicit signed fundamental cycle has boundary zero and is primitive. The regular T_q facet lattice is projective, its Hom restriction multiplies by exactly 2^q, so Ext^1_T is cyclic of this order and the restricted class generates. A W-equivariant signed augmentation has composite 2^q, giving the matching upper bound over W. Executable finite signed-action checks support but do not substitute for the proof.

originality.rationale: Full-text BWW 2005 gives the nonequivariant inflation wedge and a characteristic-zero equivariant statement, while 2026 Ayzenberg–Khoroshavkina studies ordinary inflation homotopy, and 2020 Ayzenberg–Rukhovich studies restricted functoriality. None inspected states this canonical integral group-ring extension order; actual published-finding corpus searches returned no equivalent claims. Residual risk: the same norm-group-ring extension may occur in unindexed homological algebra literature.
residual_risks: Unindexed equivalence in classical integral permutation modules or group-cohomology computations could subsume this explicit signed-norm extension.
The 2026 and earlier primary literature has been read in relevant full-text sections, but completeness of all unpublished work cannot be guaranteed.

value.rationale: For a natural infinite family of vertex-inflated simplex boundaries, the extension has a sharp exponentially growing integral obstruction despite a previously known nonequivariant wedge and rational symmetry splitting. This identifies an exact integral lattice phenomenon and a concrete boundary for what the published equivariant inflation formula can infer.
